description:
## Current delivery contract — user-approved two-outcome stack
Owner: PR A. One PR per complete outcome, NOT one PR per bead. Keep detailed beads and cohesive internal commits for tracking; consolidate existing draft foundations into their owning feature PR where practical. PR B stacks on independently usable PR A. Include owning PR documentation and validation there. This supersedes earlier per-bead/prerequisite PR instructions and historical comments. Closed foundation status is not outcome acceptance.
New-feature E2E requires explicit human UX approval in zaq-emb.12; no self-approval.

Persistent consolidated feature E2E, PR A partition. Author only after explicit .12 human approval. Reuse history.spec.js/people.spec.js; cover nonmention retained without response, shared/thread authorized views, manual/provider-grant independence and revocation, communication-channel access UI, supported refresh/unsupported/denied states, legacy history/ratings/attachments/traces preserved. Email recipient evolution and hidden Bcc exclusion use real integration tests where browser adds no value. No live execution/cursor/synchronization requirement in A. Describe actual supported providers honestly; fixtures are not proof of live provider wiring. Include results in A. Preserve assertions; no internal broad mocks.

comments.text: Authorized PR A browser suite authored in existing history.spec.js after recorded .12 approval. New persistent E2E fixture uses real Engine capture/permissions/merge/rating APIs (no broad internal mock). Covers passive nonmention with no assistant response; shared list/detail and inherited thread root; provider/manual grants, failed supported refresh preserving provider access, manual revoke/restore; unsupported refresh; merged replicated owner and aggregate ratings; restricted legacy attachments/traces; non-super-admin denial. New journeys pass 4/4 and full existing history.spec.js passes 8/8 on Chromium. Component/LiveView regressions pass 35/35. Final rerun remains required after clean PR A branch consolidation.
